option_description: Whether secrets (API keys, passwords, tokens, SSH/private keys, connection strings) are hardcoded in plaintext in source, config files, or IaC manifests committed to version control.
security_impact: Primary OR-trigger for the exposure "Hardcoded plaintext secrets in config/IaC committed to VCS" — when true, plaintext credentials are recoverable from git history and leak wholesale (ATT&CK T1552.001 Credentials in Files).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Scan the repository (working tree and history) for verified secrets.
how_to_obtain.command: trufflehog git file://. --results=verified,unknown   # or: docker run trufflesecurity/trufflehog github --repo <url>
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Zero verified secrets (secure). Any verified API keys/tokens/passwords found in tracked files or history = insecure.
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Infrastructure as Code Security Cheat Sheet

how_to_obtain.instruction: Scan the full git history with a second secret scanner to confirm no credentials are embedded.
how_to_obtain.command: git secrets --scan-history   # or: detect-secrets scan --all-files
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No secrets detected across working tree and history (secure); flagged credentials = insecure.

option_description: Whether a secret-scanning guard (pre-commit hook and/or CI scan) is installed and enforced to catch secrets before they are committed (shift-left).
security_impact: Detective/preventive control whose absence enables the exposure "Hardcoded plaintext secrets in config/IaC committed to VCS" — with no scanning guard, secrets can be committed freely; an enabled scanner is the gate that keeps that exposure from firing.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the pre-commit config to confirm a secret-scanning hook is configured.
how_to_obtain.command: cat .pre-commit-config.yaml   # confirm a detect-secrets / gitleaks / git-secrets hook is configured
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A secret-scanning hook (detect-secrets/gitleaks) present and required (secure). Absent (insecure).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the CI pipeline also runs a secret scan that gates merge, not only the local pre-commit hook.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A CI job (trufflehog/gitleaks/GitGuardian) runs on every PR and blocks merge on findings (secure). No CI-side scanning (gap).

option_description: Whether secrets are present in environment variables / .env files or baked into container image layers (docker ENV/ARG, build args).
security_impact: Primary OR-trigger for the exposure "Secrets in environment variables / .env or baked into image layers" — when true, secrets are readable by processes, logs, crash dumps, metadata endpoints, and anyone with the image (ATT&CK T1552.001).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Walk the image layers and ENV for secret strings.
how_to_obtain.command: docker history --no-trunc <image>   # and inspect image layers / env for secret strings
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No secret values present in any image layer or ENV (secure). 'Mounts must be mounted in by the orchestrator and never built-in, as this will leak the secret with the container definition.'

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check for world-readable .env files in the repo/working tree.
how_to_obtain.command: ls -l .env   # and: grep -rIl -E '(API_KEY|SECRET|PASSWORD|TOKEN)=' .
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No tracked .env carrying live secrets (secure). Plaintext credentials in .env / env files (insecure).

option_description: Whether secrets are injected at runtime by the orchestrator (sidecar, in-memory mounted volume, env-from-secret-ref) rather than built into container images or shipped in the artifact.
security_impact: Protective property whose absence (false) is an OR-trigger for "Secrets in environment variables / .env or baked into image layers" — runtime injection keeps secrets out of image layers; baked-in secrets leak with the container definition (ATT&CK T1552.001).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect image layers/ENV to confirm secrets are mounted at runtime, not built in.
how_to_obtain.command: docker history --no-trunc <image>   # and inspect image layers / env for secret strings
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No secret values present in any image layer or ENV (secure). 'Mounts must be mounted in by the orchestrator and never built-in, as this will leak the secret with the container definition.'

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the deployment manifests to confirm secrets resolve from a secret-ref / mounted volume at runtime.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Manifests use secretKeyRef / volume mounts / sidecar injection rather than literal values (secure). Inline literal secrets in manifests (insecure).

option_description: Whether secrets live in a centralized vault / secret manager (HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault, GCP Secret Manager, CyberArk Conjur) with fine-grained per-secret access rather than in flat config files.
security_impact: Protective property; its absence (false) is an OR-trigger for "Secrets in environment variables / .env or baked into image layers" — a managed store with per-secret access is the alternative to secrets kept in flat config / .env (ATT&CK T1552.001).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm config references a vault/secret-manager rather than inline values.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Evidence config references a vault/secret-manager (e.g. Vault path, AWS Secrets Manager ARN, Key Vault reference) rather than inline values (secure). Inline plaintext = insecure.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm a populated managed secret store is the documented source of truth.
how_to_obtain.command: aws secretsmanager list-secrets   # or: vault kv list secret/   (confirm a managed store is the source of truth)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A populated managed secret store exists and is the documented source of secrets (secure).

option_description: Whether all infrastructure-as-code and configuration is tracked in version control with mandatory peer-reviewed pull requests (branch protection) before merge.
security_impact: Protective change-control property; its absence (false) is an OR-trigger for "Configuration / IaC tampering with no change detection or change control" — without required review, config changes reach production with no approval or provenance (ATT&CK T1565.001 / T1195.001, NIST CM-3).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query branch protection for the required approving-review count on the default branch.
how_to_obtain.command: gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/branches/main/protection --jq '.required_pull_request_reviews.required_approving_review_count'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: >= 1 required approving review with protection enabled (secure). No branch protection / direct pushes allowed (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Infrastructure as Code Security Cheat Sheet

option_description: Whether config/IaC changes carry verified provenance via signed commits and signature-verified artifacts/components (NIST CM-14).
security_impact: Protective integrity property; its absence (false) is an OR-trigger for "Configuration / IaC tampering with no change detection or change control" — unsigned commits/artifacts let unverified infrastructure changes reach production (ATT&CK T1195.001, NIST CM-14).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm required signatures on the default branch and that commits verify.
how_to_obtain.command: gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/branches/main/protection --jq '.required_signatures.enabled'   # and 'git log --show-signature'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Required signatures enabled / commits show 'Good signature' (secure). Unsigned commits accepted (insecure).

option_description: Whether integrity monitoring / change detection is in place so unauthorized modification of config/IaC is detected (includes IaC misconfiguration scanning in CI on every change).
security_impact: Protective property; its absence (false) is an OR-trigger for "Configuration / IaC tampering with no change detection or change control" — with no integrity monitoring an attacker can weaken controls silently (ATT&CK T1565.001).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm an IaC misconfiguration/integrity scanner runs and gates CI on every change.
how_to_obtain.command: checkov -d .   # or: tflint ; tfsec . ; snyk iac test .
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Scanner runs in CI with no unresolved high/critical misconfigurations (secure). Scanner absent or findings ignored (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Infrastructure as Code Security Cheat Sheet

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm config-change events are recorded so tampering is detectable after the fact.
how_to_obtain.command: vault audit list   # AWS: confirm CloudTrail captures secretsmanager:GetSecretValue events
how_to_obtain.expected_output: At least one enabled audit device / CloudTrail data events for secret reads (secure). None (insecure).

option_description: Whether read/write access to secret stores and config is least-privilege and per-principal — engineers and services do not have blanket access to all secrets.
security_impact: Protective property; its absence (false) is an OR-trigger for "Over-broad write access to config and secret stores" — wildcard IAM/Vault policies let one compromised principal read or rewrite everything (ATT&CK T1098, NIST CM-5).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review IAM/Vault policies for wildcard access to secret stores.
how_to_obtain.command: aws iam simulate-principal-policy / review IAM policies for secretsmanager:* on Resource '*'   # Vault: review policy paths
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Policies scope each principal to specific secret ARNs/paths (secure). Wildcard secretsmanager:* on '*' or all-vault-paths (insecure).

option_description: Whether IAM roles/policies are scoped to specific secrets/paths per principal rather than granting access to an entire secret namespace.
security_impact: Protective granularity property; its absence (false) is an OR-trigger for "Over-broad write access to config and secret stores" — broad wildcard access to all secrets/config widens blast radius on one compromised principal (ATT&CK T1098).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm policies bind principals to specific secret ARNs/paths, not wildcards.
how_to_obtain.command: aws iam simulate-principal-policy / review IAM policies for secretsmanager:* on Resource '*'   # Vault: review policy paths
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Policies scope each principal to specific secret ARNs/paths (secure). Wildcard secretsmanager:* on '*' or all-vault-paths (insecure).

option_description: Whether who/what accessed which secret or changed which config, and when, is recorded in an audit trail to enable detection and incident response.
security_impact: Detective property; its absence (false) is an OR-trigger for "Over-broad write access to config and secret stores" (no audit trail means over-broad access goes unobserved) and supports detection of "Configuration / IaC tampering with no change detection or change control" (ATT&CK T1098 / T1565.001).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm audit logging is enabled on the secret store / config-change events.
how_to_obtain.command: vault audit list   # AWS: confirm CloudTrail captures secretsmanager:GetSecretValue events
how_to_obtain.expected_output: At least one enabled audit device / CloudTrail data events for secret reads (secure). None (insecure).

option_description: Whether secrets and sensitive config are encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM minimum) with envelope encryption and keys stored separately from the data they protect.
security_impact: Protective property; its absence (false) is an OR-trigger for "Config and secrets unencrypted at rest or in transit" — plaintext secrets at rest or keys co-located with data expose credentials directly.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the secret store encrypts with a managed CMK / Vault seal backend.
how_to_obtain.command: aws secretsmanager describe-secret --secret-id <id> --query KmsKeyId   # confirm CMK encryption; Vault: confirm seal/transit backend
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A KMS key id present / Vault seal configured (secure). No encryption / default plaintext storage (insecure).

option_description: Whether all retrieval of secrets and config from their store is over TLS, with no plaintext (HTTP) transport of credentials.
security_impact: Protective property; its absence (false) is an OR-trigger for "Config and secrets unencrypted at rest or in transit" — any http:// secret-store endpoint exposes credentials on the wire.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm a valid TLS handshake to the secret-store endpoint and that clients use https only.
how_to_obtain.command: openssl s_client -connect <secret-store-host>:443 </dev/null   # confirm TLS; verify clients use https:// endpoints only
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Valid TLS handshake; clients configured with https endpoints (secure). Any http:// secret-store endpoint (insecure).

option_description: Whether IaC state (e.g. Terraform state), which can contain plaintext secrets, is stored in an encrypted, access-controlled backend and not committed to VCS.
security_impact: Protective property bridging two exposures; its absence (false) is an OR-trigger for "Config and secrets unencrypted at rest or in transit" and relates to "Publicly exposed config / IaC and embedded secrets" — unencrypted or VCS-committed state leaks the plaintext secrets it holds (ATT&CK T1552.001).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm state is not tracked in VCS and the backend is encrypted + access-controlled.
how_to_obtain.command: git ls-files | grep -E 'terraform\.tfstate'   # confirm state not tracked; verify backend encryption/access on the bucket
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No state file tracked in VCS; backend encrypted + access-controlled (secure). State committed / unencrypted (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Infrastructure as Code Security Cheat Sheet

option_description: Whether a current, documented, version-controlled baseline configuration exists reflecting the most restrictive mode consistent with operations (NIST CM-2/CM-6).
security_impact: Protective property; its absence (false) is an OR-trigger for "Insecure default settings shipped to production" — with no defined baseline there is nothing to harden against and configuration is ad-hoc (OWASP A05).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm an approved, version-controlled baseline spec exists and deviations are documented.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: An approved baseline spec exists, is reviewed at a defined frequency, and deviations are documented/approved (secure). No baseline (insecure).

option_description: Whether shipped default accounts and default passwords have been removed or changed before production.
security_impact: Protective property; its absence (false) is an OR-trigger for "Insecure default settings shipped to production" — default credentials left live are trivially exploitable (OWASP A05, ATT&CK T1078.001).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm no default accounts/passwords remain in the production configuration.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No default accounts/passwords, no sample/debug endpoints, error handling does not leak stack traces, unnecessary features disabled (secure). Any present (insecure).

option_description: Whether the configuration enables only mission-essential functions, with unnecessary ports, protocols, services, and software prohibited or removed (least functionality, NIST CM-7).
security_impact: Protective property; its absence (false) is an OR-trigger for "Insecure default settings shipped to production" — unused/legacy services, ports, and protocols left enabled widen the attack surface (OWASP A05, CIS Control 4).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm configuration restricts functionality to essential capabilities; unused services/ports disabled.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Configuration restricts functionality to essential capabilities; unused services/ports disabled (secure). Unnecessary services/ports enabled by default (insecure).

option_description: Whether debug mode and verbose error messages (stack traces, exposed admin/debug endpoints) are disabled in production.
security_impact: Protective property; its absence (false) is an OR-trigger for "Insecure default settings shipped to production" — verbose errors and debug endpoints leak internal detail attackers reuse (OWASP A05).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm production error handling does not leak stack traces and debug endpoints are off.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No default accounts/passwords, no sample/debug endpoints, error handling does not leak stack traces, unnecessary features disabled (secure). Any present (insecure).

option_description: Whether sample applications, default content, and unnecessary pre-installed features have been removed from the production deployment.
security_impact: Protective property; its absence (false) is an OR-trigger for "Insecure default settings shipped to production" — sample apps and default content are well-known, frequently vulnerable footholds (OWASP A05).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm sample/default applications and content are absent from production.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No default accounts/passwords, no sample/debug endpoints, error handling does not leak stack traces, unnecessary features disabled (secure). Any present (insecure).

option_description: Whether running configuration is continuously compared against the reviewed baseline and unmanaged drift is detected and alerted (NIST CM-6 monitoring).
security_impact: Protective property; its absence (false) is an OR-trigger for "Configuration drift from the reviewed baseline undetected" — without drift detection the running config silently diverges from the hardened baseline (ATT&CK T1562.001).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Run a drift check against the baseline and confirm deviations are surfaced.
how_to_obtain.command: terraform plan -detailed-exitcode   # exit 2 = drift; or AWS Config / driftctl scan
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Plan exit code 0 (no drift) or drift surfaced and triaged via tooling (secure). No drift detection in place (insecure).

option_description: Whether the live running configuration currently matches the reviewed, hardened baseline with no unmanaged deviations.
security_impact: State property; a false value is an OR-trigger for "Configuration drift from the reviewed baseline undetected" — running config diverging from the baseline reintroduces vulnerabilities the baseline removed (ATT&CK T1562.001).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Compare running config against the baseline via a plan/scan; any drift indicates a mismatch.
how_to_obtain.command: terraform plan -detailed-exitcode   # exit 2 = drift; or AWS Config / driftctl scan
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Plan exit code 0 (no drift) or drift surfaced and triaged via tooling (secure). No drift detection in place (insecure).

option_description: Whether manual / out-of-band configuration changes are prohibited or controlled, so changes flow through the reviewed change-control workflow rather than ad-hoc hotfixes.
security_impact: Protective property; its absence (false) is an OR-trigger for "Configuration drift from the reviewed baseline undetected" — manual hotfixes and out-of-band changes are the primary source of silent drift (ATT&CK T1562.001, NIST CM-3).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review change-management procedure and confirm manual console changes are barred or reconciled back to IaC.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Out-of-band changes prohibited or reconciled into IaC under change control (secure). Ad-hoc console/manual changes routine (insecure).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Cross-check for unmanaged changes by running a drift scan.
how_to_obtain.command: terraform plan -detailed-exitcode   # exit 2 = drift; or AWS Config / driftctl scan
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Plan exit code 0 (no drift) or drift surfaced and triaged via tooling (secure). Unmanaged out-of-band changes show as drift (insecure).

option_description: Whether the repository holding config/IaC is private rather than a public git repo.
security_impact: Protective property; its absence (false) is an OR-trigger for "Publicly exposed config / IaC and embedded secrets" — a public repo discloses configuration and any embedded secrets to unauthenticated attackers (ATT&CK T1530).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the repo is private and check for any public exposure of config artifacts.
how_to_obtain.command: aws s3api get-bucket-policy-status --bucket <b> --query PolicyStatus.IsPublic   # and: curl -s https://<host>/.env ; ls -l .env
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Bucket IsPublic=false, .env returns 404/403 from web and has 0600 perms, repo private (secure). Any public exposure (insecure).

option_description: Whether config files (e.g. .env) have restrictive filesystem permissions and are not world-readable or web-served.
security_impact: Protective property; its absence (false) is an OR-trigger for "Publicly exposed config / IaC and embedded secrets" — world-readable .env / config files disclose embedded secrets locally and over the web (ATT&CK T1530).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check config file permissions and that .env is not served over the web.
how_to_obtain.command: aws s3api get-bucket-policy-status --bucket <b> --query PolicyStatus.IsPublic   # and: curl -s https://<host>/.env ; ls -l .env
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Bucket IsPublic=false, .env returns 404/403 from web and has 0600 perms, repo private (secure). Any public exposure (insecure).

option_description: Whether object-storage buckets holding config/IaC are private and not publicly accessible.
security_impact: Protective property; its absence (false) is an OR-trigger for "Publicly exposed config / IaC and embedded secrets" — an open S3/object-storage bucket discloses configuration and embedded secrets (ATT&CK T1530).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the bucket policy status reports the bucket is not public.
how_to_obtain.command: aws s3api get-bucket-policy-status --bucket <b> --query PolicyStatus.IsPublic   # and: curl -s https://<host>/.env ; ls -l .env
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Bucket IsPublic=false, .env returns 404/403 from web and has 0600 perms, repo private (secure). Any public exposure (insecure).

option_description: Whether the cloud instance metadata endpoint is restricted (e.g. IMDSv2 / hop-limit / no SSRF reachability) so config and credentials it exposes cannot be harvested.
security_impact: Protective property; its absence (false) is an OR-trigger for "Publicly exposed config / IaC and embedded secrets" — an exposed metadata endpoint discloses configuration and instance credentials (ATT&CK T1530).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Probe the instance metadata endpoint to confirm IMDSv2 is required and credentials are not freely reachable.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/   # then confirm IMDSv2 token is required (HttpTokens=required)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: IMDSv1 unauthenticated access blocked; token required (secure). Credentials retrievable without a token (insecure).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm instance metadata options enforce required tokens and a low hop limit across the fleet.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Instances set HttpTokens=required and HttpPutResponseHopLimit=1 (secure). Optional/v1-allowed metadata (insecure).

option_description: Whether IaC state files (which can hold plaintext secrets) are not committed to a public repo or stored in a publicly accessible backend.
security_impact: Protective property; its absence (false) is an OR-trigger for "Publicly exposed config / IaC and embedded secrets" — publicly exposed state leaks the plaintext credentials it contains (ATT&CK T1530 / T1552.001).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm state is not tracked in VCS and the backend is not publicly accessible.
how_to_obtain.command: git ls-files | grep -E 'terraform\.tfstate'   # confirm state not tracked; verify backend encryption/access on the bucket
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No state file tracked in VCS; backend encrypted + access-controlled (secure). State committed / unencrypted (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Infrastructure as Code Security Cheat Sheet

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the state backend bucket is not public.
how_to_obtain.command: aws s3api get-bucket-policy-status --bucket <state-bucket> --query PolicyStatus.IsPublic
how_to_obtain.expected_output: IsPublic=false on the state backend bucket (secure). Public state backend (insecure).

option_description: Whether configuration is recoverable to a known-good state via VCS history and a documented restore path.
security_impact: Protective property; its absence (false) is an OR-trigger for "No config backup or rollback to a known-good state" — without a known-good copy, tampering, deletion, or ransomware leaves nothing to restore (ATT&CK T1485).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm a documented restore path to a prior reviewed commit exists.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Documented restore path: revert to a prior reviewed commit + restore secret store/state from backup (secure). No recovery path (insecure).

option_description: Whether the secret store and IaC state are backed up and restorable, complementing VCS history for full configuration recovery.
security_impact: Protective property; its absence (false) is an OR-trigger for "No config backup or rollback to a known-good state" — VCS history alone cannot restore secret-store/state contents after loss (ATT&CK T1485).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the secret store and state backend are backed up and restorable per the documented recovery procedure.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Documented restore path: revert to a prior reviewed commit + restore secret store/state from backup (secure). No recovery path (insecure).

option_description: Whether the rollback / restore-to-known-good procedure has been actually tested, not just documented.
security_impact: Assurance property; its absence (false) is an OR-trigger for "No config backup or rollback to a known-good state" — an untested rollback path may fail when needed, leaving the system unrecoverable after tampering or loss (ATT&CK T1485).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm a rollback/restore drill has been performed and evidenced (date, result), not merely documented.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Evidence of a successful restore test (revert to prior commit + restore secret store/state) within a defined period (secure). Untested or never-exercised procedure (gap).
